scholarships.title: UBC International Scholars Program
scholarships.official_source: The University of British Columbia (UBC) Undergraduate Admissions

existing.description: UBC's International Scholars Program offers two prestigious awards to high academic achievers who are dedicated to giving back to their communities.
eligibility: You are an international student who will be studying in Canada on a Canadian study permit.
You are entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school.
Applicants for 2027 Winter session must have graduated from high school no earlier than June 2026.
You are applying for your first undergraduate degree.
You can prove a significant level of financial need.
Your family is not able to afford a significant level of your educational costs and does not have access to external funding.
You meet UBC's admission requirements, including general and degree-specific requirements.
You demonstrate superior academic achievement (achieve all As or equivalent standard).
You meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard, or the English language requirement for UBC Vantage College if applying through Vantage One.
You are nominated by your high school or a qualifying registered non-profit organization.
You provide a reference from an academic referee who is a different person from your nominator.
existing.eligibility_summary: International students entering UBC directly from an accredited secondary school for a first undergraduate degree, with all As or equivalent and a documented significant level of financial need, who are nominated by a high school or qualifying non-profit and meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard by January 31.
benefits: Financial support determined by assessed financial need, described as the amount representing how much support you would require to live and study at UBC after all your resources are accounted for
For the Vantage One Excellence Award only, value stated as ranging up to the full cost of a student's academic program and living expenses
Dedicated advising and support from International Scholars Program advisors
coverage: Financial support determined by assessed financial need, described as the amount representing how much support you would require to live and study at UBC after all your resources are accounted for
For the Vantage One Excellence Award only, value stated as ranging up to the full cost of a student's academic program and living expenses
Dedicated advising and support from International Scholars Program advisors
requirements: Submit a completed UBC Admissions application before starting the award application; the award application requests confirmation of UBC application submission.
Be nominated by one nominator (guidance counsellor, principal, administrator, etc.).
Provide a teacher referee who is a different person from the nominator.
A high school or registered non-profit organization may nominate up to two students for UBC Vancouver (including Vantage College), and one student for UBC Okanagan.
The nominator and teacher referee recommendations need to be completed and submitted a few days before November 15.
You cannot complete your award application until both the nominator and teacher referee forms have been completed and submitted.
Complete the in-depth financial information sections: annual income and expenses, family wealth and assets, dependents and annual school fees, and sources of financial support.
Calculate family contributions and financial need using UBC's cost estimator.
Complete 4 essay questions of approximately 150-250 words each.
Complete a video interview if invited; you will have one week to record your responses on the online application platform.
Submit any admission documents required to evaluate your UBC application by January 31, not the date listed in the 'Your UBC Application – Next Steps' email.
Meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard by January 31.
documents: Official documents that demonstrate your financial need
Documents outlining your family's gross income, expenses, and family assets
Annual income and expenses information entered in the application
Family wealth and assets information entered in the application
Details of dependents and annual school fees
Sources of financial support entered in the application
Awards already held, listed in the application
Nominator's completed and submitted nomination form
Teacher referee's completed and submitted reference form
4 written essay responses of approximately 150-250 words each
Records of any required documents to evaluate your UBC application, submitted to the UBC Undergraduate Admissions Office
Transcripts and high school academic certificates
Official English language test results, if an English language test is required
existing.english_requirement: You must meet UBC's English Language Admission Standard. If you do not satisfy this requirement for direct entry, you may be eligible for UBC Vantage College and the Vantage One Excellence Award, which requires the English language requirement for UBC Vantage College. If you are required to take an English language test, you must complete the test early enough for UBC Admissions to receive your official test results by January 31.
application_method: Decide on your academic program and campus (for the awards you are considered for your first choice program; you should still select a second choice program).
Discuss the nomination with your school and confirm your high school is able to nominate you.
Submit your UBC Admissions application (required before the award application can be started).
Email your nominator and teacher referee requesting their recommendations and give them your first choice campus and program.
Create your award application account and invite your nominator and teacher referee to complete their forms.
Gather financial and supporting information and complete your sections of the award application.
Have the nominator and teacher referee complete and submit their forms a few days before November 15.
Submit your completed award application by November 15.
Submit required admission documents and English language results by January 31.
Complete the video interview if invited (one week to complete).
Check your email, including spam filters, for updates; results are released on a rolling basis February to April 2027.
existing.selection_notes: UBC states there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria. As part of the evaluation process a financial assessment is carried out, reviewing documents outlining family gross income, expenses and family assets. Applicants are assessed on demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, and outstanding academic performance (all As or equivalent standard). Applicants may be invited to a video interview to share more about themselves and reflect on past educational and leadership experiences beyond the written application. You do not select which award you wish to receive; the team automatically considers you for the awards you are eligible for. Applicants who apply to the International Scholars Program will not be considered for merit-based awards.
existing.best_fit: International students completing secondary school outside Canada who will enter UBC Vancouver or UBC Okanagan directly from an accredited secondary school for their first undergraduate degree, hold an all-As or equivalent record, can document a significant financial need, and can secure a nomination from a high school or qualifying registered non-profit.
existing.notes: Non-renewable status, deferral and return-home requirements are not published on the programme page. There is no published clinical restriction, but the following degrees are explicitly not eligible for UBC International Scholars Program awards: Bachelor of Nursing degree (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management degree, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions. Applicants may only be considered for either UBC's merit-based or its financial need-based award programme. Applicants must hold a Canadian study permit. Applicants started shortly before the deadline are less likely to be successful. Housing should not be applied for until award decisions are released, because the housing application deadline is May 1.
existing.application_period: Opens October 5, 2026 and closes November 15, 2026 (11:59 p.m. PST) for the September 2027 intake. Supporting admission documents and English language results due January 31, 2027. Video interviews January to March 2027. Results released on a rolling basis February to April 2027, with decisions confirmed by early to mid-April 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for the September 2027 intake will open on October 5, 2026. The International Scholars Program application is due November 15 (11:59 p.m. PST). Required admission documents and proof of meeting UBC's English Language Admission Standard are due January 31, 2027.
